text:
maya: FYI saw intermittent tail spikes when host staging starts evicting large KV sets. 20-60ms tails, looks correlated with nvme IO peaks.
maya: Repro: mixed gen+embed load, model quantized, batch 6.
cheng: Paste iostat? suspect queue saturation + synchronous page-ins.
maya: nvme1 util 92%, await ~30ms.
anuj: Short-term controls: per-tenant concurrent page-in limit + adaptive prefetch. Avoid touching allocator for now.
sarah: Strong prefer soft per-tenant budgets vs kill-switch global throttle so premium tenants stay protected.
kyle: Danger: allocator metadata held across page-in can deadlock if we throttle. We need non-blocking wait paths or handoff.
jon: We need telemetry: page_in_q_depth_by_tenant + tenant_pagein_latency_p95.
infra-bot: alert: staging-nvme-saturation at 1723456700 correlated with heavy offload batches.
cheng: Plan: quick experiment in staging-3. runtime hysteresis controller clamps page-in concurrency when host_io_pct > 70%.
cheng: staging flags:
offload.page_throttle_pct: 0.65
offload.prefetch_budget: 5
anuj: Safety: if page-in p95 > 50ms for 30s, set prefetch=2 and immediately prefer smaller model variant for that tenant.
sarah: Also emit metrics to console: tenant_prefetch_budget, tenant_pagein_p95_ms, host_nvme_util_pct.
kyle: I'll convert the page-in path to release allocation mutex before waiting; use optimistic refcounts + waiter queue. Small PR.
jon: Scope rollout: staging-3 -> staging-wide -> 5% prod canary. Who owns staging run?
cheng: I'll own rollout and dashboard. 24h run with eval prompt set.
maya: If experiment looks good, capture tradeoffs in short RFC (latency vs fragmentation vs cpu/io cost).
anuj: I'll draft longer-term interface RFC to expose per-tenant offload budget and pluggable throttle policies (hysteresis, AIMD, leaky-bucket).
maya: Action items: cheng deploy flags, kyle allocator tweak PR by EOD, anuj RFC by Fri, sarah dashboards. Add regression prompt set for prefetch changes.
jon: Add failure-mode notes (prefetch too low -> quality regression) so Optimize can warn.
maya: Thanks, moving to staging testing.
